title: Chapter 16
content:
The next day, Kang Seok-joo dragged him to a prefabricated low-rise building sitting dead in the center of Seoul. From the street, the three-story structure looked like any ordinary commercial photography studio.

Once past the reinforced doors, however, it was virtually identical to the underground den from two nights ago. The only difference: the room was partitioned into glass display booths, each housing a half-naked man or woman stripped down to their underwear.

A private peep show. It immediately reminded Jakyeong of the antique censer and crown locked away in Kang Il-hyun’s subterranean vault—precious relics showcased under glass.

A short distance from the booths, low tables were strewn with half-empty champagne flutes, charcuterie boards, loose prescription pills, and discarded syringes. Most of the patrons were already blasted out of their skulls on booze and narcotics.

Glass in hand, Seok-joo ambled between the booths, a sleazy smirk plastered across his face, before coming to a dead stop in front of one of the men. Staring at the conspicuous bulge pressing against the front of the model's briefs, Seok-joo turned and held his forearm out toward Jakyeong.

"Yi-an, come look at this! This dude is packing an absolute monster. Jesus, is he actually Korean?"

Dumping pills on top of liquor had clearly turned the kid's tongue to lead.

Breezing past the male booth, Seok-joo stopped in front of a woman. Catching his eye, she pressed her bare breasts flush against the glass and dragged her tongue slowly across the pane. Seok-joo plucked the cigarette from his lips and began licking the glass from the outside, tracing her cleavage.

Two tongues writhed against opposite sides of the transparent divider, slathering the glass in a thick smear of saliva. Taking it a step further, the woman dipped her fingers into her mouth, coating them with spit, before slipping a hand beneath her lace panties to stroke herself.

That pushed Seok-joo past his breaking point. His face flushed red, and he spun around to Jakyeong, his breath coming in ragged gasps.

"Fuck, man. I'm rock-hard right now."

"..."

"What do you think? If you like her, you can take her first. Or... we could just run a threesome."

"I'll pass."

"Cool. Wait right here, I'll be back in a minute."

Jakyeong gave a docile nod.

Seok-joo immediately turned around and whistled for someone. A handler hurried over—sides of his head shaved clean, hair pulled back into a slick topknot, his entire body plastered in tattoos from the collarbone down, with metal studs glinting from his ears and septum.

Seok-joo whispered in his ear. Moments later, the glass door clicked open, and the woman in lace lingerie and stiletto heels sashayed out, hooking her arm possessively around Seok-joo's.

As the pair vanished up the stairs toward the private suites, the handler lingered, eyeing Jakyeong up and down.

"You're Seok-joo's friend, right? Don't see any girls catching your eye? Don't worry about the tab—Seok-joo's covering the damage."

"No, thank you... I'm good."

"Ah. Different tastes, then?"

The handler pointed toward the muscular man in the adjacent booth. The model was lazily pinching his own nipple between his thumb and forefinger, licking his bottom lip before shooting Jakyeong a deliberate, slow wink.

Jakyeong forced a thin, strained smile. "No. Not that either."

"Younger, then?"

When Jakyeong didn't answer, the man leaned close, his voice dropping into a conspiratorial purr.

"Just say the word. I've got kids barely past ten."

Jakyeong turned his head, staring straight into the handler's eyes. The man was grinning, eagerly awaiting a nod of approval.

Jakyeong gave a slow, firm shake of his head. Disappointment flickered across the handler's face; he muttered that Jakyeong should sleep on it, then sauntered off to service another patron. Around the room, drunken trust-fund brats were leading hand-picked models upstairs one by one.

Slipping through the hedonistic haze, Jakyeong stepped out into the foyer and surveyed the perimeter. The main gates were locked tight from the inside, and Kang Il-hyun’s surveillance detail was almost certainly parked somewhere along the avenue outside. Clearly on edge after the close call two nights ago, Il-hyun had assigned a tail.

Jakyeong had spotted the black sedan shadowing them the entire drive over, though Seok-joo had been too oblivious to notice a thing. Is the kid just brain-dead, or does he genuinely not give a shit?

Brushing the thought aside, Jakyeong slipped back into the lounge, snatched an unattended dark jacket and ballcap from the back of an empty sofa, and slipped out the side exit.

Rounding the building, he reached the rear perimeter wall. Scaling the chest-high brick barrier in a single fluid vault, he checked both directions of the narrow back alley. Empty—no surveillance cameras, no pedestrians. He dropped lightly onto the asphalt below.

Keeping low, he navigated the rear lanes, spotting the surveillance sedan idling near the main street. Darting between parked cars in their blind spots, he melted into the city grid without triggering an alarm. At a 24-hour convenience store down the block, he purchased a disposable black face mask, flagged down an empty taxi, and handed the driver a handwritten slip of paper.

The cabbie glanced at the scrap, then waved his hands in immediate refusal. "Ah, hell no. That's way too far out. I can't take you there, buddy."

Jakyeong reached into his wallet, pulled out a thick stack of 50,000-won banknotes, and slapped them straight into the driver's palm.

The taxi shifted into drive instantly.

Throughout the ride, the driver repeatedly eyed Jakyeong through the rearview mirror, clearly unnerved by a silent passenger masked up and bundled in a pulled-down cap.

Even late at night, Seoul's main arteries were packed with traffic. After nearly an hour of driving, the cab veered off the expressway, weaving deeper into a dense, decaying market district. It was an enclave heavily populated by foreign laborers—dimly lit, damp, and raw, with drunkards screaming and brawling outside dingy dive bars along every block.

"Looks like we're right around here," the driver muttered.

Right on cue, the navigation system chimed, announcing they had arrived in the vicinity of their destination. The moment the tires stopped rolling, Jakyeong popped the door and stepped out into the night air. Behind him, the taxi sped off down the narrow alleyway as if escaping a crime scene.

Jakyeong checked the live coordinates on his phone. This was the exact first stop logged by the GPS tracker he’d planted under Choi Ki-tae’s sports car. The log indicated Ki-tae had idled here for about ten minutes before moving on. The alleys were an intricate, tangled maze, making precise satellite tracking fuzzy, but the target zone was definitely within this block.

Sticking an unlit cigarette between his lips, he began walking at a measured pace. Dilapidated eateries and flickering neon signs lined the damp street.

After circling a few blocks, a car parked outside a 24-hour convenience mart caught his eye. A man in a black tank top stepped out of the mart, carrying a plastic bag as he walked toward the vehicle.

Jakyeong recognized the face instantly. The mugger who held a blade to my ribs.

The man slid into the passenger seat, and the vehicle took a sharp right turn fifty feet ahead. Tugging his ballcap lower, Jakyeong fell into step behind them.

The car crawled through the narrow corridor before pulling up in front of a two-story multi-family brick house. Jakyeong slipped into the deep shadows between two adjoining buildings.

Two men exited the vehicle—the tank-top thug lingered by the bumper checking his phone, while a man with a shaved head bounded up the exterior stairs.

Moments later, the second-floor door banged open. Curses and barking orders echoed down the stairwell, followed by the hurried patter of footsteps.

One, two, three, four, five, six, seven.

Seven kids—boys and girls ranging anywhere from ten to twenty years old—shuffled down the concrete steps in single file.

"Hurry the fuck up, move!" the shaved thug barked from above.

Near the iron gate, the smallest boy in the group tripped and went sprawling across the gravel. The thug in the tank top immediately stepped forward, kicking the boy hard in the ribs. As the child's scrawny frame skidded across the dirt, a teenage girl rushed forward from the back of the line, hauling the crying boy to his feet.

By her oversized jacket and worn sneakers, Jakyeong recognized her instantly: the drop-runner from the alleyway.

The kids were herded into the back of a large black passenger van. The heavy sliding door slammed shut with a sharp clack, and the van began rolling slowly forward.

Leaning the back of his head against the brick wall, Jakyeong let out a long, quiet sigh. He reached for his lighter, then paused, shoved it back into his pocket, and sprinted down the parallel alleyway.

Having committed the street layout to memory, he anticipated their route. Bursting out onto a wider thoroughfare, headlights cut through the gloom as the black van rounded the corner, cruising downhill toward him.

Jakyeong stumbled into the center of the lane, deliberately blocking their path.

The van screeched to a halt.

The shaved driver rolled down his window, leaning his neck out with a feral snarl. "Get out of the fucking road, you crazy bastard!"

Staggering like a belligerent drunk, Jakyeong dragged his feet toward the sliding rear door and yanked it open. A row of terrified young faces stared back at him.

"Mister! Daerim-dong!" Jakyeong slurred in a drunken drawl.

The tank-top thug in the passenger seat kicked his door open, charging around the front bumper with a curse. Reaching out to drag Jakyeong away by the collar, he lunged—only for Jakyeong’s boot to lash out in a devastating front-kick.

CRACK!

The sickening crunch of a shattered nasal bone ripped through the air as the man was thrown violently onto his back, shrieking in agony.

Realizing things had gone sideways, the shaved driver vaulted out of the front cab. Jakyeong slipped into the driver’s seat like water, slammed the shifter into gear, and stomped on the throttle. The driver lunged frantically to grab the door handle, but his grip slipped on the accelerating frame, sending him crashing onto the pavement.

Accelerating fifty yards down the alley, Jakyeong slammed the brakes.

In the rearview mirror, the two thugs were scrambling back to their feet, roaring with venomous rage as they charged after the van.

Jakyeong glanced over his shoulder at the kids huddled in the back. "Close the door."

While the younger children froze in terror, the teenage girl stepped up, grabbing the handle and sliding the heavy door shut until it latched tight.

Jakyeong slammed the transmission into reverse. "Hold on to something."

The two men were sprinting flat-out, closing the gap to thirty feet—twenty feet—

Jakyeong floored the gas pedal in reverse.

The heavy van surged backward like a charging bull. Caught completely off guard, the two men had no time to dive out of the way before the steel bumper plowed into them with a brutal, bone-crushing THUD.

The impact shuddered through the entire chassis. The kids shrieked in unison.

Catching sight of the two bodies rolling across the asphalt in the rearview mirror, Jakyeong offered the trembling children a casual, deadpan apology.

"Sorry about that. My driving's a little rusty."

He tapped the gas in reverse once more. The rear tires bumped up and over something soft with a sickening crunch, accompanied by raw, bloodcurdling screams. Glancing in the side mirror, both thugs were writhing in the dirt, clutching pulverized legs.

"Tch. Heads are still intact."

He considered putting the car in drive to finish the job and crush their skulls properly, but porch lights were already flicking on across the residential block. Down the road, restaurant staff and patrons were spilling out into the alley, murmuring in alarm.

Jakyeong clicked his tongue in mild disappointment. That's enough for tonight. No point wasting all my energy on the opening act.

Leaving the mangled thugs groaning in the dirt for another day, he shifted into drive and gunned the van through the labyrinth of alleys, disappearing into the city night.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Daerim-dong (대림동): A well-known neighborhood in southwestern Seoul with a large population of Chinese immigrants, Korean-Chinese (Joseonjok), and vibrant ethnic food markets. In Korean noir and crime media, it is often depicted as a gritty, high-intensity cultural hub.

  • 50,000-won Note (오만원권): The highest-denomination banknote in South Korea (featuring Shin Saimdang), roughly equivalent to $35 - $40 USD per bill. Tossing several to a cabbie is the Korean equivalent of dropping a stack of hundred-dollar bills to bypass rules.
